- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67) — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2%.  
- If last 3–5 days show mean reversion (prices falling after rising), model often fails to correct — add 1–3% downward bias for next 3–5 days.  
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with model lag — if sentiment shifts sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transition.
